stem:
Meena throws a ball straight up into the air in her school playground. The ball slows down, stops for a moment, and then falls back to the ground, speeding up as it comes down.
Which statement correctly explains the motion of the ball?

options.text: The Earth pulls the ball towards itself with an attractive gravitational force, which slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down.
The ball carries an upward force from the throw until this force runs out, and the Earth pulls the ball only after it starts falling.
The Earth's gravitational force acts only when the ball is touching the ground, so the ball slows down on its own while going up.
The Earth pushes the ball upwards while it rises and pulls it downwards only at the highest point.

teacher.key_rationale: Earth's gravity is attractive, acts without contact, and acts on the ball throughout its flight: it decelerates the upward motion and accelerates the downward motion, matching option A. Options B, C and D each encode a common misconception (thrown force persists / gravity needs contact / gravity reverses direction).
